title: Security review - Data residency & region pinning
next_steps: Jordan to share region-pinning architecture and EU-only pilot plan by 2026-12-24
Samir to provide KMS integration guide and options for customer-managed keys (CMK) by 2026-12-27
Schedule follow-up legal deep-dive on DPA, SCCs, and Schrems II mitigations for week of 2026-12-29
action_items: Jordan Lee - share region pinning architecture doc by 2026-12-24
Samir Patel - send KMS/CMK integration examples and retrofit checklist by 2026-12-27

summary: Redwood and BlueHarbor reviewed data residency controls and region pinning options for a US/EU-sensitive POC. Customer requires EU-only processing for PHI-derived telemetry and wants options for customer-managed keys, audit logs, and a clear sub-processor list. Discussed routing, SCCs, SSO/RBAC integration, and Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted for residency guarantees. Agreed next steps: share architecture docs, KMS guidance, and schedule legal follow-up.
topics: Data residency requirements and EU-only processing
Cross-border transfers and SCCs / Schrems II considerations
Customer-managed keys (KMS) and encryption at rest
transcript:
00:00:05 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We have Samir (our SE) and Aisha (security PM) with me. How's everyone?
00:00:12 Lisa Carter: Hi, Lisa here. Appreciate you making time. We wanted this to be pretty focused on residency and legal constraints - especially EU processing for our clinical telemetry.
00:00:25 Miguel Santos: Yeah, hi. Miguel - infra. Quick note, we run a split stack, EU for PHI, US for analytics, we want to avoid any cross-border telemetry leakage.
00:00:38 Samir Patel: Great, thanks. We'll walk through region pinning, routing, and keys. I'll start with a high level of how Redwood handles region pinning. Apologies in advance if I mis-say things - sometimes our autoprops transcriber changes names.
00:00:51 Samir Patel: So, Redwood supports pinning workloads to regions - you can choose EU-only model endpoints for inference. For hosted customers we offer region-level tenancy; for Dedicated you get reserved pools in your VPC or our dedicated infra.
00:01:07 Priya Rao: When you say "hosted EU-only" - are there guarantees that telemetry never leaves EU? We have contractual and regulatory needs.
00:01:15 Aisha Khan: Good question. For hosted EU endpoints we route requests to EU regions physically, and we can restrict storage of logs/metrics to the region. That said, depending on features like global analytics and cross-region failover, there are configurations that might replicate limited metadata. We recommend Dedicated or Private for full guarantees.
00:01:38 Lisa Carter: So Dedicated is the safe route - but can you explain the delta: is it network isolation, or legal contract changes?
00:01:47 Samir Patel: It's both. Dedicated gives you compute pools reserved for your org, isolated network, and we can turn off cross-region telemetry. For hosted, we provide soft guarantees and operational defaults. Contractually, Dedicated customers can get stronger SLA and data residency wording in the DPA.
00:02:05 Evan Brooks: What about subprocessors - e.g., do you use third-party logging or observability that processes outside EU?
00:02:12 Aisha Khan: We maintain a sub-processor list and can provide it. Core infra in EU uses the cloud provider's EU regions (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west1, etc.). Some ancillary services may be US-based by default; for Dedicated we can swap to EU equivalents or enable on-prem collectors. We'll share the sub-processor inventory.
00:02:33 Miguel Santos: Important - can we get the full list now or in writing? We need to run it through procurement.
00:02:38 Jordan Lee: We'll attach the latest sub-processor export after the call.
00:02:42 Lisa Carter: Thanks. On cross-border transfers - do you rely on SCCs or other transfer mechanisms?
00:02:49 Samir Patel: We rely on the standard EU SCCs in our DPA and have template clauses. For some customers we offer additional technical controls - e.g., EU-only KMS CMKs, strict logging in-region, and blocking fallback to US regions. Note: Schrems II risks are mitigated by minimizing transfers and providing technical controls, but legal team will need to sign off.
00:03:12 Priya Rao: We need to understand whether metadata or telemetry for model prompts could ever be routed to US for model routing or cache warmups.
00:03:21 Samir Patel: For the EU-pinned model endpoints, primary inference and KV cache are in-region. However, if you enable cross-region fallbacks or global batching for cost efficiency, there is a small chance of routing. We can disable global batching for your POC.
00:03:39 Lisa Carter: Okay that's helpful. Encryption - we want CMK with customer control. Can you support customer-managed keys?
00:03:46 Aisha Khan: Yes. We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we offer KMS options where you can bring your CMK in supported cloud providers, and a limited bring-your-own-key flow. We'll send the KMS integration guide with examples for AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault.
00:04:05 Miguel Santos: With CMK, who holds the key material? We want non-access by vendor ops.
00:04:11 Samir Patel: Key material stays in your KMS. Redwood holds references and uses envelope encryption. For Dedicated we can implement key encryption/decryption flows that require customer-side key operations for key unwrap. We'll supply the architecture diagram.
00:04:27 Lisa Carter: Audit logs - we need immutable audit logs for access and admin actions. Retention 7 years. Can you guarantee immutability and export?
00:04:36 Jordan Lee: We provide audit logs with configurable retention. For Dedicated/Private customers we can set longer retention and allow syslog/S3 export to your tenant-controlled storage. Immutability can be achieved via WORM-enabled buckets and legal hold policies. We'll include export examples.
00:04:55 Evan Brooks: Do audit logs include token-level breakdown or only high-level?
00:05:00 Aisha Khan: We can provide token-level cost/latency breakdowns, but by default we obfuscate PII. For your use case we'll propose a sanitized telemetry feed and a separate admin audit feed - both can be restricted to the EU region.
00:05:17 Priya Rao: SSO and RBAC - we need SCIM user provisioning, SAML 2.0, and role separation aligned with our internal IAM. How does that map to your product roles?
00:05:27 Samir Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, plus role-based roles in the console (admin, developer, auditor). For Dedicated, we can map to your IdP groups and implement fine-grained RBAC and just-in-time provisioning. We'll send a mapping template.
00:05:44 Lisa Carter: Great. A little concerned about telemetry used for model improvements - do you ever use customer prompts or outputs for training?
00:05:51 Aisha Khan: No training on customer data unless you opt in. We have an opt-in mechanism for logs used in model tuning, otherwise data is only used for service operation and quality monitoring with strict retention. We'll put the policy section in the doc.
00:06:09 Miguel Santos: On the technical side, if we go Dedicated in EU, what are typical latencies vs hosted global? We have tight SLAs for some endpoints.
00:06:19 Samir Patel: Latencies are comparable to regional hosted endpoints; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower jitter. We can run a benchmark for your payloads - recommended next step: a controlled POC in eu-west-1 with sample prompts.
00:06:33 Jordan Lee: We'll propose a POC: EU-only Dedicated pool for two weeks, run 100k tokens/day, measure latency and costs. Agreed?
00:06:41 Lisa Carter: Sounds good but need legal sign-off first.
00:06:44 Priya Rao: Yes, legal will review DPA and SCCs. Also need written confirmation about sub-processors, retention, and access controls.
00:06:53 Samir Patel: We'll add a secure link to the sub-processor list and DPA templates. Note: our DPA includes SCCs and standard EU clauses; for enterprise customers we can negotiate additional clauses.
00:07:06 Evan Brooks: One question: do you ever use third-party model providers that might be outside EU? e.g., we heard you sometimes route to different model variants for cost.
00:07:15 Aisha Khan: We primarily serve models from our catalog within the pinned region. We can restrict to EU-only model variants. If a fallback is configured, we would notify and you can disable fallbacks.
00:07:29 Miguel Santos: About logs and PII - we want redact-at-ingestion. Is there a built-in PII scrubber?
00:07:36 Samir Patel: We have optional redaction and PII-scrubbing pipelines you can enable. They run in-region if enabled for EU. For Dedicated, we can deploy custom regex or ML based scrubbing.
00:07:49 Lisa Carter: Excellent. Can you confirm retention windows for different telemetry types?
00:07:55 Aisha Khan: By default: operational logs 90 days, audit logs 1 year. For Dedicated enterprise we can extend to your requested 7 years for audit logs and 3 years for metrics. We'll put configurable retention controls in the doc.
00:08:11 Priya Rao: On contractual terms: we want explicit clause about no sub-processor transfers without notice and 30 day review. Is that typical?
00:08:20 Jordan Lee: We can include a notification clause and a 30-day review period in enterprise DPA adds. We'll flag that for the Legal team.
00:08:28 Evan Brooks: From an ops perspective, if we run into a failover and the EU region is down, what happens? Do you fail to US or queue?
00:08:36 Samir Patel: For critical workloads we recommend Dedicated with regional redundancy inside EU (multiple EU regions) and a policy to fail to a secondary EU region only. We can disable US fallback entirely. For hosted customers with global routing, failover may route elsewhere unless disabled.
00:08:56 Lisa Carter: Okay. A couple more specifics: 1) Can we get an exportable list of admins and access events daily? 2) Does Redwood redact logs in the backup lifecycle?
00:09:07 Aisha Khan: 1) Yes, daily admin activity exports to your S3 in EU. 2) Backups follow the same retention and redaction policies; for Dedicated we can ensure backups never leave EU.
00:09:20 Priya Rao: Also, can we get the SOC 2 and ISO certs and last audit dates?
00:09:25 Jordan Lee: Absolutely - we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs and the last audit summary.
00:09:31 Miguel Santos: On encryption in transit - TLS only? Any mTLS options?
00:09:36 Samir Patel: TLS 1.2+ in transit. For Dedicated we can support mTLS for service-to-service communication and client certs for internal APIs. We'll include an mTLS deployment option in the guide.
00:09:49 Lisa Carter: Great. One risk item: Schrems II. If you rely on SCCs, are there additional technical measures?
00:09:56 Aisha Khan: We implement supplementary technical measures when requested: minimizing transfers, CMK, in-region logging, and contractual safeguards. Legal team will need to review and sign off on mitigations.
00:10:08 Jordan Lee: Quick recap before we go deeper in legal: items we'll share - sub-processor list, DPA + SCCs template, region pinning architecture diagram, KMS/CMK integration guide, audit/export examples, and SOC/ISO certs.
00:10:21 Lisa Carter: That works. We'll review with procurement and legal and circle back.
00:10:25 Priya Rao: Please also send us a sample DPA redlines doc so we can propose edits.
00:10:29 Jordan Lee: Will do.
00:10:33 Samir Patel: Anything else technical we should cover now?
00:10:36 Evan Brooks: One small thing - do you provide a list of sub-processors with location tags (EU/US)?
00:10:42 Aisha Khan: Yes we'll include region tags per sub-processor entry.
00:10:46 Lisa Carter: Perfect. Thanks team. If legal is comfortable we'll plan the EU Dedicated pilot.
00:10:52 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and set the legal deep-dive.
00:10:56 [End of recorded portion - meeting continued off-camera with legal and procurement housekeeping, small talk about holidays and scheduling.]

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings ("autoprops" vs "autopros"), product name variances ("Redwood Dedicate" etc.). Shared artifacts: DPA template (link: https://redwood.ai/security/dpa-template), Region pinning doc (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/region-pinning), KMS integration guide (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/kms-integration).
